newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs close sharply lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs close sharply lower on profit-taking.

text.p: After successive rises, Brazilian shares ended sharply lower Tuesday on profit-taking and speculative trades, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 48 most traded stocks closed off 2.2 percent at 11,110 points. Volume was high at 862.7 million reais ($813.8 million).

Some traders had expected the market, particularly Telebras, to lose ground after the bolsa's continued sharp rally. Telebras rose over 21 percent in May, which led some investors to move to second-tier stocks on Monday.
"The market took a breather after the recent surge in Telebras stock prices," a broker said.
Some analysts also noted that the bolsa began to suffer from speculation ahead of the June 16 options settlement. while its common stock fell 2.79 percent to close at 136.10 reais.
Other blue-chips also posted losses. State oil firm Petrobras fell 1.2 percent to 247 reais, while private miner Companhia Vale do Rio Doce dropped 1.28 percent to 23.20 reais.
Federal power holding firm Eletrobras dropped 2.07 percent to 520 reais.
Despite Eletrobras' nosedive, Sao Paulo's power sector index closed up 0.13 percent at 2,845 points, with reais.

Banespa shares surged for the second day in a row. The state bank's preferred rose 21 percent to 19.30 reais. Trade in the bank resumed Monday after a seven-day suspension pending the conclusion of a debt restructuring deal with the federal government.
Playes on Wednesday are likely to focus on the much- awaited announcement of the qualified bidders for the Band B cellular selloff, brokers said.
Qualified bidders are expected to be announced at 0900 local/1200 GMT.
